ps_conjecture.source: M. Petrache, S. Serfaty, Crystallization for Coulomb and Riesz interactions as a consequence of the Cohn-Kumar conjecture
ps_conjecture.text: Conjecture 1 (Cohn-Kumar [CK]). In dimension d = 2, 8, resp. 24, the lattice Lambda_0 is universally minimizing in the sense that it minimizes E_p among all possible point configurations of density 1 for all p's that are completely monotone functions of the squared distance. ... Then Conjecture 1 was recently proved in dimensions 8 and 24 — it remains open in dimension 2.

ck_cm_def.source: H. Cohn, A. Kumar, Universally optimal distribution of points on spheres, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 20 (2007), 99-148
ck_cm_def.text: Recall that a C^infinity function f : I -> R on an interval I is completely monotonic if (-1)^k f^(k)(x) >= 0 for all x in I and all k >= 0 (see [Wid, p. 145]) ... It might seem preferable to use completely monotonic functions of distance, rather than squared distance, but squared distance is in fact more natural than it first appears ... it is more general than using distance: it is not hard to prove that if r -> f(r^2) is completely monotonic on a subinterval (a,b) of (0,infinity), then f is completely monotonic on (a^2,b^2), but not vice versa.

sal_defs.source: D. S. Salazar, Bernstein Functions at Work: Coalescents, Copulas, and Subordination
sal_defs.text: Definition 2.1 (Completely monotone, Bernstein, and Stieltjes classes). Let all functions below be defined on (0, infinity) and take values in [0, infinity). (i) A function f is completely monotone, written f in CM, if f in C^infinity and (-1)^n f^(n)(x) >= 0 for every n >= 0 and x > 0. ... (ii) A function g is a Bernstein function, written g in BF, if g in C^infinity and g' in CM.

sal_bw.text: Theorem 2.3 (Bernstein-Widder). f in CM if and only if there is a unique positive Radon measure mu on [0, infinity) such that f(x) = integral over [0,infinity) of e^(-xt) dmu(t).

sal_subord.text: This dictionary - Bernstein-Widder for CM functions, Levy-Khintchine for Bernstein functions, and Bochner subordination for their composition - turns many analytic questions into statements about a representing measure that one can often write down explicitly [31, 19]. (Reference [31] there is R. L. Schilling, R. Song, Z. Vondracek, Bernstein Functions: Theory and Applications, 2nd ed., de Gruyter, 2012; the statement that a completely monotone function composed with a Bernstein function is completely monotone is NOT quoted there and its theorem number in [31] was not verified by us.)

mathlib_am_def.source: Mathlib, Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/AbsolutelyMonotone.lean (Michael R. Douglas, 2025), pinned Mathlib d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612
mathlib_am_def.text:
def AbsolutelyMonotoneOn (f : ℝ → ℝ) (s : Set ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ p : ℝ → FormalMultilinearSeries ℝ ℝ ℝ,
    HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn ∞ f p s ∧
    ∀ (n : ℕ) ⦃x : ℝ⦄, x ∈ s → 0 ≤ p x n fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)
